clue.text: Extra-hearty lettuce is back in city

indicators.note: is back tells us the built word is read from right to left
an extra heart means the middle letter of the word is doubled

parts.note: lettuce is the basis of a salad, so it stands for the word salad

explanation.surface: A city is praised for its unusually robust lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra-hearty' doubles the central L of SALAD to give SALLAD, and 'is back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a large city in Texas, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: A hairstyle, one pound less — that's charming

indicators.note: less means that letter is taken away

parts.note: a mullet is a haircut short at the front and long at the back
L stands for one pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A haircut that costs a pound less is such a delight.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn for protection, so it is something that charms.

clue.text: Sweet fellow that holds up all the traffic

definitions.text: Sweet fellow that holds up all the traffic

parts.note: a lollipop is a sweet on a stick
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A kind man brings the whole road to a standstill.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a school crossing patrol carries a round stop sign on a pole, resembling a giant lolly, to halt cars for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A school crossing patrol stops all the vehicles with a round sign shaped like a lolly.

clue.text: Rush away, fly — on horse?

indicators.note: on here means the fly is set within the saddle

parts.note: the question mark points to what sits on a horse, its saddle
a ked is a wingless fly that lives on sheep

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to flee on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: A ked (sheep ked) is a parasitic fly; it goes inside SADDLE, the thing on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is a colloquial verb meaning to run off hurriedly.

clue.text: Lands round front of green: God! About seven feet for an eagle

definitions.text: About seven feet for an eagle

indicators.note: round says the first word goes around the next piece

parts.note: lands as in gains or secures, a sense of wins

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of the word green

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A golfer shouts in delight on landing near the green, then the clue turns to birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The golfing words (green, eagle) set up a course, but the eagle is the bird and the definition is its measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: A wingspan is the tip-to-tip width of outstretched wings, about two metres in a golden eagle.

clue.text: The three of us in London said to be Presbyterian

indicators.note: a Cockney accent turns the th sound into f, so the phrase sounds different in London

parts.note: a trio including the speaker is we three

explanation.surface: A trio of friends in the capital are rumoured to be Presbyterians.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech turns 'th' into 'f', so WE THREE becomes WEE FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Free Church of Scotland, a Presbyterian body, are nicknamed this.

clue.text: New to a person's service

parts.note: one's means belonging to a person

explanation.surface: A newcomer is introduced to someone's church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Nones is a daily office of prayer said at the ninth hour, a church service.

clue.text: No time for deck-chair-one may be pounding the beach

definitions.text: one may be pounding the beach

indicators.note: no means the time abbreviation is left out

parts.note: a deckchair is a type of seat

explanation.surface: No time to relax in a deckchair while waves crash ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea's waves pound the shore, so it is something that may be pounding the beach.

clue.text: White man went over province — he made notes

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means sitting above the next piece

parts.note: an albino lacks pigment, so is a white man
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A pale man travelled across a province.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is called 'the Province' in Britain; in a down answer 'went over' puts ALBINO above NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomaso Albinoni was a Venetian baroque composer, so he made musical notes.

clue.text: Give it one's best shot?

parts.note: read literally, the best shot in darts or archery is the one hitting the centre of the target

explanation.surface: An encouragement to try as hard as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullseye is the centre of a target, the spot a perfect shot strikes.

clue.text: Mean to run tailender out and close

parts.note: mean in the sense of stingy, also near in British usage

indicators.note: tailender out removes the final letter of the word for a run

parts.note: a bye is a run scored in cricket without the batter hitting the ball

explanation.surface: A cricket captain plans to run out the last batsman, ending the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: a bye is a run conceded when the ball passes the batter and keeper; a tailender is a weak late-order batter. Here 'tailender out' drops the last letter of BYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Close in the sense of not far away is a synonym for the adverb nearby.

clue.text: Holy city famed in all parts

indicators.note: parts means the answer is made of parts of these words, hidden across them

explanation.surface: A holy city celebrated throughout the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Medina in Saudi Arabia is the second holiest city in Islam, burial place of the Prophet.

clue.text: Girl, sort of drip, almost embraced by Pole

indicators.note: embraced by puts the shortened word inside the pole

parts.note: a rod is a pole or stick

indicators.note: almost cuts the final letter from the word

parts.note: a saline drip is a kind of drip used in hospitals

explanation.surface: A girl, rather a wet type, is nearly hugged by a man from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality but is a rod; 'sort of drip' is SALINE, and 'almost' trims it to SALIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosalind is a girl's name, for instance the heroine of As You Like It.

clue.text: Beat one promising streetwalker in the evening

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
a plighter is one who plights, or pledges

explanation.surface: A thug beats a prostitute who is making promises at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streetwalker' suggests a prostitute, but the lamplighter walked the streets at dusk lighting gas lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamplighter walked the streets each evening lighting gas lamps.

clue.text: Edition of most talented writing

indicators.note: an edition is a version, so these words are issued in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A collection of work by the most gifted authors is published.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament is the first part of the Christian Bible, sacred scripture or writings.

clue.text: Competitor in marquee with a number of bonds

indicators.note: in puts the competitor inside the marquee

parts.note: a marquee is a large tent
a rival is a competitor

explanation.surface: A contestant is in a big tent with several financial bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivalent atom has a valency of three, forming three chemical bonds.

clue.text: South American countess broke the hearts of noble kings

indicators.note: broke means the countess breaks in between those letters
the hearts of takes the centre letter of each of the two words

parts.note: Olivia is the countess in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night

explanation.surface: A Latin American countess left aristocratic monarchs heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: The hearts of 'noble' and 'kings' are B and N; 'broke' puts OLIVIA between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Bolivia, a country in South America, is a South American.

clue.text: Potential item? It's a very old story

definitions.meaning: an item is a couple, and a first meeting of two young people may become one
the stock romantic plot, told countless times

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a first romantic encounter and the oldest plot in fiction.

clue.text: Anger man put into verse

parts.note: a strop is a bad temper or fit of anger
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man's rage is turned into poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A strophe is a stanza or section of a poem, a unit of verse.

clue.text: Judge view to be in contention

parts.note: an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: A judge's opinion is up for debate.
explanation.definitionFit: To jangle in an old sense is to quarrel or wrangle, so to be in contention.

clue.text: Red conspirator brought to prisoner's place

parts.note: Cinna was one of the conspirators against Julius Caesar
the bar is where the accused stands in a courtroom

explanation.surface: A communist plotter is taken to the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a political label for the conspirator but is the definition, a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is a mercury ore whose name also means a vivid scarlet colour.

clue.text: Don't agree with party …

explanation.definitionFit: Beano is British slang for a lively party, and split it reads be a no, refuse.

clue.text: Golden tree needing laborious cleaning?

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the gean is the wild cherry tree

explanation.surface: A gilded tree is so filthy it needs a great deal of scrubbing.
explanation.walkthrough: AU is gold's chemical symbol; the gean is the European wild cherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Augean recalls the stables of King Augeas, cleaned by Hercules, so it means extremely filthy.

clue.text: Writing English arrested at a public event abroad

indicators.note: arrested means the abbreviation is held inside the word for writing

parts.note: fist is an old informal word for handwriting

explanation.surface: An English writer is arrested at a public gathering overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festival or holiday celebration in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: … have interview with Salisbury, for one

definitions.meaning: to meet and talk with someone
Salisbury is the seat of a bishop's diocese

explanation.definitionFit: To see someone is to meet them; a bishop's diocese is called by this word.

clue.text: Highly-regarded exercise involving wild tigers

indicators.note: involving means the exercise abbreviation wraps around the jumbled letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: wild means the letters of tigers run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: An esteemed fitness class with untamed big cats.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun used attributively, as in 'a prestige brand', so it stands fairly for 'highly-regarded'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige used as an adjective describes something of high status, as in a prestige car.

clue.text: Work in eleven parts that may bear your stamp

indicators.note: in places the work abbreviation inside the jumbled letters
parts suggests the word eleven is broken up and reassembled

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A piece of music composed in eleven sections bearing your mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work in eleven parts' suggests a musical composition; the definition hides at the end. 'in' sets OP inside ENVELE, the rearrangement 'parts' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter's paper cover carries a postage stamp, so it may bear your stamp.

clue.text: Holder of first course originally called dull routine gets backing

indicators.note: gets backing means the joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: née introduces a woman's original name
a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: A dull routine that was once called something else is now supported.
explanation.definitionFit: A tureen is a deep serving dish for soup, the usual first course.
